'''''Veronica elliptica''''', [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] '''''Hebe elliptica''''', is a plant of the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Plantaginaceae]].<ref name="POWO_811951-1">{{citation |title=''Veronica elliptica'' G.Forst. |work=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:811951-1 |access-date=2022-10-09 }}</ref> It is native to New Zealand (including the [[New Zealand Subantarctic Islands|Antipodean Islands]] and the [[Chatham Islands]]), [[Patagonia]] and the [[Falkland Islands]].<ref name=POWO_811951-1/> It is an evergreen, bushy shrub of 1 m or more in height, with green, oval leaves, 2–4 cm long. Flowers are white to pale mauve.{{citation needed|date=October 2022}}

Branches from plants of ''Veronica elliptica'' on [[Disappointment Island]], [[Auckland Islands]], New Zealand were used by the survivors of the shipwreck of the ''[[Dundonald (ship)|Dundonald]]'' to build a [[coracle]] and [[oar]]s which they eventually used to successfully reach [[Auckland Island]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Escott-Inman |first=Herbert |url=https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q123924640 |title=The Castaways of Disappointment Island |publisher=S.W. Partridge & Co. |year=1911 |location=London |language=English}}</ref>
